title: Take-Two Boss 'Not in the Least' Concerned Bad Press Will Affect GTA 6
description: Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick says he is not in the least concerned that bad press surrounding Rockstar's employment tribunal will affect GTA 6's launch.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## Take-Two Boss 'Not in the Least' Concerned Bad Press Will Affect GTA 6

According to a recent report by gaming media outlet Eurogamer, Take-Two Interactive CEO Strauss Zelnick has stated that he is "not in the least" concerned that the negative press surrounding alleged union-busting at Rockstar Games will affect the upcoming launch of Grand Theft Auto 6.

### Addressing the Controversy

As one of the most anticipated video games in history, GTA 6 has been under a massive global spotlight. Alongside the immense hype, developer Rockstar Games has faced media attention and scrutiny regarding employment tribunals and allegations concerning union-busting. In an era where workplace conditions and employee rights are heavily scrutinized by the gaming community and media alike, such controversies can sometimes create significant PR challenges.

However, when directly confronted with concerns about whether this bad press might dampen the game's monumental launch, Zelnick remained entirely unfazed.

### Unshakable Market Confidence

Zelnick's dismissal of the potential impact reflects a broader corporate confidence in the sheer gravitational pull of the Grand Theft Auto franchise. With a massive, highly dedicated global player base eagerly waiting to dive into the next installment, management clearly believes that the underlying demand for the product eclipses external controversies.

As the release window draws closer, the industry will undoubtedly continue to monitor both the legal and employment developments surrounding Rockstar and the unstoppable commercial juggernaut that is GTA 6.

## Editor's Take

Strauss Zelnick's comments highlight Take-Two's unwavering belief in the commercial invulnerability of GTA 6. While players are primarily focused on the game itself, these ongoing labor discussions point to a growing need for major publishers to balance massive commercial ambitions with sustainable internal practices.
